title: Shimreishang Kala Maitonphi
alternate_titles: The Ballad of Shimreishang and Maitonphi
notes: Legendary 17th-century tragic romance ballad originating from Phungcham village. Documented in oral histories and theatrical works.

lines_translation: Love dwells deep in the heart of Shimreishang.
Maitonphi is the fairest flower of the land.
Beside the clear running streams of Phungcham.

lines_tangkhul: Atonphi wui sam kaphana won thada.
lines_translation: In our Phungcham village, deep affection grew.
At that sacred time, our generation was transformed by love.
Maitonphi's beauty blossomed like the wild mountain flower.

lines_tangkhul: Shimreishang na khangayei wui tui kashak.
lines_translation: Shimreishang's enduring vow of lifelong faithfulness.
Shall never fade through the turning of generations.
Under the divine gaze of the Creator, true love endures.

title: Haola: Luira Laa
notes: Ritual seed-sowing festival (Luira Phanit) ceremonial chant invoking agricultural blessings and ancestral protection.

lines_translation: At the Luira seed-sowing festival, the hills rejoice.
The auspicious celebration of our mountain homeland.
Passed down through ancient ancestral generations.

lines_tangkhul: Awunga wui kakhon aina lui kahon.
lines_translation: Led by the solemn invocation of the village chief.
The sacred seed grains are blessed across every field.
Bowing before the Creator for a bountiful harvest year.
The maidens and warriors step in traditional dance.
The finest blossoms of youth adorn our village.
Echoing across every hill and river gorge.

title: Haola: Chumpha Laa
notes: Post-harvest celebration song sung during Chumpha Phanit when granaries are consecrated.

lines_translation: At the Chumpha harvest feast, granaries are blessed.
Reaping the abundance of the terrace fields.
Beside the flowing rivers and eternal stones.
The matriarchs open and consecrate the rich granaries.
Rejoicing in the fullness of gathered autumn crops.
Sharing the festive feast in community harmony.

title: Haola: Khangrei Laa
notes: Traditional youth courting chant performed during gatherings at the Longshim (traditional youth dormitory).

lines_translation: The youth assemble at the Longshim dormitory.
The finest flowers among young men and maidens.
In that evening circle, true love awakens.

lines_tangkhul: Khangrei laawui khon kaphana kongrei thata.
lines_translation: The courting melody flows sweetly like the mountain stream.
No grief or heaviness can linger in the heart.
The radiant joy of our ancestral generation shines bright.

title: Haola: Thisham Laa
notes: Memorial lamentation chanted during Thisham, the final ancestral send-off feast for departed souls.

lines_translation: At the Thisham memorial feast, the mountain stands silent.
Honoring the departed souls in solemn reverence.
Preserving the sacred customs of our fathers and mothers.
Into the ancestral spirit realm, the soul journeys.
Guided toward the sacred heights of the celestial hills.
The loving memory of our kindred shall never fade.

title: Haola: Ngashan Laa
title_translation: Song of the Traditional Shawl and Attire
notes: Ceremonial song celebrating Tangkhul traditional woven garments (Haora, Luirim) and cultural heritage.

lines_translation: Adorned in the woven glory of the traditional Haora shawl.
Blending the rich crimson and black stripes of Luirim.
The dignity and cultural artistry of our Tangkhul land.
Woven by the skilled hands of our ancestral mothers.
Passed down through centuries as our cultural treasure.
Danced with pride across the mountain heights.

title: Haola: Mawon Laa
notes: Traditional lullaby and maternal blessing chant recorded in CIIL Tangkhul Folk Literature collection.

lines_translation: O precious little child, radiant bloom of my life.
Rest softly in peace upon your mother's breast.
The heavenly Creator shall watch over your slumber.
May wisdom and goodness guide your steps in youth.
Growing tall and noble among the children of our village.
Blossoming like the fairest flower upon our mountains.

title: The Tangkhul Folk Poetry in Song (HAOLA)
title_translation: The Tangkhul Folk Poetry in Song
notes: Comprehensive research compilation of Tangkhul oral poetry and musical chants catalogued at CIIL Bhasha Sanchika.

lines_tangkhul: Hao laawui khon kongrei thata ngaloong.
lines_translation: The melody of Hao Laa flows like an untamed mountain river.
The sacred oral poetry of our ancestral fathers and mothers.
Echoing joyous harmony through hills and forested gorges.

title: Folk Songs of the Tangkhul
notes: Published ethnographic collection documenting traditional songs, festival verses, and working chants across Tangkhul villages.

lines_translation: Chronicles of the Tangkhul people across mountain villages.
Songs sung together while cultivating terraced fields.
Gathering in the traditional dormitory in shared joy.

title: Jesuwui Laa
notes: Earliest printed songbook in the Tangkhul language (1907, American Baptist Mission, Ukhrul). Public Domain.

lines_translation: The blessed love of Jesus.
Reaching every family and dwelling.
The joyous gospel of the heavenly realm.
Firmly trusting in the will of the Creator.
Spreading the dawn of light across Tangkhul land.
Giving the eternal gift of spiritual life.

title: Christian Songs (1916)
collector: Centre for Academic Translation and Archiving (CATA)
notes: Historic 1916 compilation of Christian songs printed in Roman script, preserved in scanned form at Delhi University CATA.

lines_translation: Joy dwells in worshipping the Creator.
The good news echoes across the mountain heights.
Held steadfast within the hearts of our people.
Walking in the path of truth and righteousness.
United in the everlasting love of Jesus.
Dwelling in peace across every village of Ukhrul.

title: Saharwon Kapaiwon
notes: Acclaimed Naga folk-blues track blending traditional Tangkhul melody with acoustic guitar and folk harmonica.

lines_tangkhul: Saharwon kapaiwon, kaphungli won kapha wonri.
Choithar ramwui ningyangla, leikashi khangatei lei.
lines_translation: Saharwon gentle flower, blooming on the high mountain slopes.
Sweet delight of Choithar village, pure love unchanging through time.

title: Chihohaira
notes: Traditional celebration chant arranged into modern Naga folk-blues.

lines_tangkhul: Hao laawui khon aina pheikao kazing.
lines_translation: The call of the festival echoes, the community gathers as one.
Stepping together to the timeless rhythm of ancestral folk song.

title: Mayokachang Tam Wonrei
notes: Folk blues song evoking seasonal beauty and cultural metaphors.

lines_translation: Spring blossoms unfold in beauty across the mountain slopes.
Dwelling in harmony, our generation celebrates peaceful life.

title: Ngayang Kahai Leishat
notes: Reflective folk ballad on love, endurance, and memory.

lines_translation: Unwavering devotion abides steadfast in the depth of my heart.
Enduring across rivers and mountains in lifelong love.

title: Made in Ukhrul
notes: Highly popular anthem celebrating Ukhrul town, Tangkhul youth culture, and pride of place.

lines_tangkhul: Made in Ukhrul, kaphung ramwui yarshungwon.
Iram Tangkhul wui mashun aina ningyang.
lines_translation: Made in Ukhrul, youth blooming in the heart of our mountain town.
Taking pride in the upright dignity and culture of Tangkhul land.

title: Ningna Khamaya
notes: Contemporary romantic ballad on mutual devotion and longing.

lines_translation: The heart's gentle consent in true mutual love.
Never perishing through the years, cherished deep within.

title: Nganam Kapha Won
notes: Melodic love song employing floral imagery to represent beloved virtue.

lines_translation: Sweet-scented blossom, flowering across our ancestral hills.
Your tender love rests like light upon my soul.

title: Huinahao
notes: Contemporary folk fusion incorporating ancestral call-and-response refrains.

lines_translation: Huinahao, greetings to all, the sacred hills awaken.
Listen to the guiding voices of our mothers and fathers.

title: Iwui Mirinwui Khararchan
notes: Classic Tangkhul autobiographical ballad renowned across generations since its 1991 release.

lines_translation: The story of my life unfolds like the mountain trails.
Through sorrow and trials, the Creator has been my protector.

title: Ramreichan
notes: Homeland hymn expressing affection for the ancestral hills and valleys of Ukhrul.

lines_tangkhul: Ramreichan, iram Ukhrul wui kaphung kapha.
lines_translation: Cherished homeland Ukhrul, blessed mountain territory.
Across ridges and clear streams, love for home remains true.

title: Ngathor Zingran Thada
notes: Poetic love ballad comparing youthful affection to the first rays of mountain dawn.

lines_translation: Like the radiant morning dawn over the mountain ridges,
Your love brings warm light into every corner of my life.

title: Kharao Amei
notes: Celebrated Tangkhul duet highlighting camaraderie, affection, and mutual respect.

lines_translation: Deep spirit of friendship, rejoicing together in camaraderie.
The pure love and mutual respect of our village youth.

title: Iram Rakhongli
notes: Nostalgic folk song describing community life and meetings around the traditional village water spring.

lines_translation: At the village spring, clear sweet water flows eternal.
In that gathering place, cherished words and memories are shared.

title: Hunkhamang Mikumo Mirin
notes: Philosophical ballad on the impermanence of mortal life and moral uprightness.

lines_translation: Fleeting and brief is mortal human life on this earth.
Walk therefore in truth, honor, and kindness across your homeland.

title: Ramna Ngateida
notes: Song expressing homesickness and thoughts of homeland while living far away.

lines_translation: Though living far in distant lands across rivers and plains,
My heart longs forever for the misty hills of Ukhrul.

title: Longkata Chara
notes: Soulful ballad describing sorrow, parting, and tears.

lines_translation: Tears that fall in silent moments of parting and grief.
Yet the enduring bond of love remains undefeated.

title: Achanwon
notes: Modern romantic track addressing a beloved by name.

lines_translation: Achanwon beloved, calling your name brings joy to my spirit.
Blossoming like the fairest flower upon our mountain home.

title: Awon Thada Rakhawon
notes: Poetic song praising natural beauty and youthful blossom.

lines_translation: Blossoming like the spring flower, your gentle love arrives.
Bringing festival happiness into our mountain realm.

title: Chingri Kahai
notes: Introspective song exploring quiet contemplation and personal resilience.

lines_translation: In the peaceful stillness of the mountain ridge, deep wisdom speaks.
Holding steadfast faith, bowing before the Almighty Creator.

title: Mailemphy
notes: Romantic tribute song celebrating traditional maiden grace.

lines_tangkhul: Tangkhul ngalanao wui mashun themthot pamei.
lines_translation: Mailemphy beloved, your radiant grace illuminates our hills.
Embodying the gentle modesty and upright virtues of Tangkhul maidens.

title: Phadang Village Harvest Chant
notes: Candidate oral recording of a Phadang village harvest chant; pending primary audio archive session verification and dialect gloss confirmation.

lines_translation: Across the fertile paddy fields of Phadang village, the harvest chant echoes.
Pure waters flowing as the golden crops are reaped.
The enduring prosperity and peace of Phadang homeland.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 1: Ili Jesuna Laishi
title_translation: Jesus Loves Me in Tangkhul Naga
lyricist: Anna Bartlett Warner (Original) / Rev. William Pettigrew (Trans.)
composer: William B. Bradbury (Tune 1155 | Doh is E)
notes: Hymn No. 1 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907, American Baptist Mission, Ukhrul). 5 stanzas translated by Rev. William Pettigrew from the original hymn 'Jesus Loves Me'.

lines_translation: Jesus loves me, this I know,
For the Bible tells me so;
Little ones to Him belong,
They are weak, but He is strong.
Yes, Jesus loves me,
The Bible tells me so.
Jesus loves me, He who died,
Heaven's gate to open wide;
He will wash away my sin,
Let His little child come in.
Jesus loves me, loves me still,
Though I'm very weak and ill;
From His shining throne on high,
Comes to watch me where I lie.
Jesus loves me, He will stay,
Close beside me all the way;
Thou hast bled and died for me,
I will henceforth live for Thee.
Jesus loves me, when I die,
He will take me home on high;
Trusting in His precious grace,
Dwelling in that heavenly place.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 2: He Jesuwui Makali Ringphalaka
alternate_titles: Safe in the Arms of Jesus (Tangkhul)
title_translation: Safe in the Arms of Jesus in Tangkhul Naga
composer: William H. Doane (Tune 57 | Doh is G)
notes: Hymn No. 2 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907, American Baptist Mission, Ukhrul). 2 stanzas translated into classical archaic Tangkhul orthography.

lines_tangkhul: Awui ngahan ngaida romhai, Phasa kakhanang rai.
Kachingwui chan nganalu, Iwui la sada laili,
Jesuna nani mashitta, Hangda la kasana.
lines_translation: Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe on His gentle breast;
There by His love o'ershadowed, sweetly my soul shall rest.
Hark, 'tis the voice of angels, borne in a song to me,
Over the fields of glory, over the jasper sea.
Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe from corroding care;
Free from the blights of sorrow, free from the tempter's snare.
Free from the doubts and conflicts, in that blissful realm above,
Where mortal grief and sin no more can sever us from love.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 3: Jesuwui Vang Nganinglu
alternate_titles: Stand Up, Stand Up for Jesus (Tangkhul)
title_translation: Stand Up, Stand Up for Jesus in Tangkhul Naga
lyricist: George Duffield Jr. (Original) / Rev. William Pettigrew (Trans.)
composer: George J. Webb (Tune 680 | Doh is Bb)
notes: Hymn No. 3 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 3 stanzas translated by Rev. William Pettigrew celebrating moral steadfastness.

lines_translation: Stand up, stand up for Jesus, ye soldiers of the cross;
Lift high His royal banner, it must not suffer loss.
From victory unto victory His army shall He lead,
Till every foe is vanquished, and Christ is Lord indeed.
Stand up, stand up for Jesus, the trumpet call obey;
Forth to the mighty conflict in this His glorious day.
Ye that are men now serve Him against unnumbered foes;
Let courage rise with danger, and strength to strength oppose.

lines_tangkhul: Aja gung gung kang gang sali,
lines_translation: Stand up, stand up for Jesus, the strife will not be long;
This day the noise of battle, the next the victor's song.
To him that overcometh, a crown of life shall be;
He with the King of Glory shall reign eternally.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 4: Jesuwui Aming Ngasoda
alternate_titles: Take the Name of Jesus with You (Tangkhul)
title_translation: Take the Name of Jesus with You in Tangkhul Naga
composer: William H. Doane (Tune 91 | Doh is Ab)
notes: Hymn No. 4 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 4 complete stanzas on spiritual comfort and peace.

lines_translation: Take the name of Jesus with you, child of sorrow and of woe;
It will joy and comfort give you, take it then where'er you go.
Precious name, O how sweet! Hope of earth and joy of heaven;
Precious name, O how sweet! Hope of earth and joy of heaven.
Take the name of Jesus ever, as a shield from every snare;
If temptations round you gather, breathe that holy name in prayer.
O the precious name of Jesus! How it thrills our souls with joy,
When His loving arms receive us, and His songs our tongues employ.
At the name of Jesus bowing, falling prostrate at His feet,
King of kings in heaven we'll crown Him, when our journey is complete.

title: Itang Rakhongli
alternate_titles: Song of the Riverbank and Beloved Hills
title_translation: Song of the Riverbank and Beloved Hills
notes: Classic Tangkhul lyrical love song expressing yearning across mountain ranges, invoking the hills to lower their peaks that one may gaze upon beloved homeland.

lines_translation: Along the riverbanks of our village, gazing far into the distant hills,
O beloved, looking far across the valleys.
Beside the clear murmuring waters and sacred ancient stones,
In my heart, the deepest love of our youth abides.
O mother, let not our tearful eyes be dimmed by distance,
Let not sorrow cloud the vision of our eyes.
The beloved mountain ridge rises tall between us,
O gentle peaks, lower yourselves down that I may gaze upon my love!
That our eyes may catch a glimpse of our beloved homeland,
The fairest blossom blooming on the slopes of Hunphun.
The sacred promise whispered in mutual longing,
Shall never perish through the passing of generations.

title: Yarra Laa: Yarshungwon
title_translation: Youth Spring Awakening and Courting Chant
collector: Dr. Ringkahao Horam / Tribal Research Institute
notes: Traditional youth spring festival chant performed during Yarra Phanit, celebrating spring blossom and mutual courting in the traditional dormitory.

lines_tangkhul: Sikui kazing thota won kapha khawon,
lines_translation: At the return of Yarra spring festival, the mountain hills awake,
The youthful maidens and young men gather to share their stories.
Wild berries ripen in the warmth of the mountain breeze,
In our Hungpung village, youthful delight abounds.

lines_tangkhul: Lui thot mashakpa rui thot kasa,
lines_translation: Before the heavy ploughing and seasonal toil begin,
Voices resonate within the halls of the traditional youth dormitory.
Like mountain rivers flowing pure beneath the spring sky,
Love and mutual admiration blossom among the youth.
Beloved daughters of our ancestral villages,
Singing songs of youthful strength and boundless joy.
Under the watchful blessing of the divine Creator,
We dance together in the graceful steps of Yarra.

title: Mangkhap Laa: Ngaphit Kazang
notes: Traditional agricultural chant sung at the culmination of rice transplantation during Mangkhap Phanit, expressing thanksgiving for communal labor.

lines_translation: At the arrival of Mangkhap festival, the arduous transplantation is fulfilled,
Across all the terraced emerald paddies of Phungcham.
Having labored together shoulder to shoulder under monsoon rain,
Today our community rejoices in hard-won rest and peace.
Honoring the sacred agrarian traditions of our fathers and mothers,
Through weeks of knee-deep mud and relentless toil.
Now the young rice shoots stand vibrant across the fields,
And every household prepares the celebratory feast of thanksgiving.
Trusting in the benevolent provision of the Almighty,
We look forward with hope to the golden harvest of autumn.
With mountain waters brimming through irrigation channels,
We share the cups of fellowship and festival joy.

title: Hao Pheichak Laa
collector: H. Kamkhenthang / Directorate of Tribals Manipur
notes: Antiphonal ceremonial warrior and celebration dance chant performed during major public gatherings and festival dances (Pheichak).

lines_translation: In the ceremonial circle of Hao Pheichak, the rhythmic footwork echoes,
The valiant defenders and sons of Longpi village step forth.
Adorned in ceremonial headgear and traditional woven shawls,
Their anthems of bravery resound through the mountain ridges.
Bearing the regal customs and nobility of our ancestral chiefs,
Shield and spear gleaming in ceremonial defense.
Against all adversities and neighboring perils,
The honor and righteousness of our people stand unshakable.
Singing the shared historical ballads and martial chants,
Joining together as one voice during the festival season.
The sacred heritage of the Tangkhul people shall never fade,
Enduring through countless generations into eternity.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 5: Jesu Nawui Ming Phaningda
alternate_titles: Jesus, the Very Thought of Thee (Tangkhul)
title_translation: Jesus, the Very Thought of Thee in Tangkhul Naga
lyricist: Bernard of Clairvaux / Edward Caswall (Original) / Rev. William Pettigrew (Trans.)
composer: John B. Dykes (Tune 60 | Doh is C)
notes: Hymn No. 5 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907, American Baptist Mission, Ukhrul). 5 stanzas translated into classical Tangkhul by Rev. William Pettigrew.

lines_translation: Jesus, the very thought of Thee
With sweetness fills my breast;
But sweeter far Thy face to see,
And in Thy presence rest.
Nor voice can sing, nor heart can frame,
Nor can the memory find
A sweeter sound than Thy blest name,
O Savior of mankind!
O hope of every contrite heart,
O joy of all the meek,
To those who fall, how kind Thou art!
How good to those who seek!
But what to those who find? Ah, this
Nor tongue nor pen can show;
The love of Jesus, what it is,
None but His loved ones know.
Jesus, our only joy be Thou,
As Thou our prize wilt be;
Jesus, be Thou our glory now,
And through eternity.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 8: Jesuwui Krushwui Pamli
title_translation: Beneath the Cross of Jesus in Tangkhul Naga
lyricist: Elizabeth C. Clephane (Original) / Rev. William Pettigrew (Trans.)
composer: Frederick C. Maker (Tune 139 | Doh is Bb)
notes: Hymn No. 8 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 4 complete stanzas translated by Rev. William Pettigrew.

lines_translation: Beneath the cross of Jesus
I fain would take my stand,
The shadow of a mighty rock
Within a weary land;
A home within the wilderness,
A rest upon the way,
From the burning of the noontide heat,
And the burden of the day.
Upon that cross of Jesus
Mine eye at times can see
The very dying form of One
Who suffered there for me;
And from my smitten heart with tears
Two wonders I confess:
The wonders of redeeming love
And all my unworthiness.
I take, O cross, thy shadow
For my abiding place;
I ask no other sunshine than
The sunshine of His face;
Content to let the world go by,
To know no gain nor loss,
My sinful self my only shame,
My glory all the cross.
O Christ, who bore the bitter agony
Upon the shameful tree,
To pay the debt of all my sins
And set my spirit free;
Bearing the sorrows of the world
That we may live in light,
Lord, in Thy grace let me abide,
Made holy in Thy sight.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 9: Arui Chimik Tunra
title_translation: Now the Day Is Over in Tangkhul Naga
notes: Hymn No. 9 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 7 stanzas translated by Rev. William Pettigrew.

lines_translation: Now the day is over,
Night is drawing nigh;
Shadows of the evening
Steal across the sky.
Now the darkness gathers,
Stars begin to peep;
Birds and beasts and flowers
Soon will be asleep.
Jesus, give the weary
Calm and sweet repose;
With Thy tenderest blessing
May our eyelids close.
Grant to little children
Visions bright of Thee;
Guard the wandering travelers
And shelter them with peace.
Through the long night watches
May Thine angels spread
Their white wings above me,
Watching round my bed.
When the morning wakens,
Then may I arise
Pure, and fresh, and sinless
In Thy holy eyes.
Glory to the Father,
Glory to the Son,
And to Thee, blest Spirit,
Whilst all ages run.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 10: Jesuwui Mi Chatsa
title_translation: Onward, Christian Soldiers in Tangkhul Naga
notes: Hymn No. 10 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 5 stanzas translated by Rev. William Pettigrew.

lines_translation: Onward, Christian soldiers,
Marching as to war,
With the cross of Jesus
Going on before.
Christ the royal Master,
Leads against the foe;
Forward into battle
See His banners go!
At the sign of triumph
Satan's host doth flee;
On then, Christian soldiers,
On to victory!
Hell's foundations quiver
At the shout of praise;
Brothers, lift your voices,
Loud your anthems raise!
Like a mighty army
Moves the Church of God;
Brothers, we are treading
Where the saints have trod.
We are not divided,
All one body we,
One in hope and doctrine,
One in charity.
Crowns and thrones may perish,
Kingdoms rise and wane,
But the Church of Jesus
Constant will remain.
Gates of hell can never
'Gainst that Church prevail;
We have Christ's own promise,
And that cannot fail.
Onward then, ye people,
Join our happy throng,
Blend with ours your voices
In the triumph song.
Glory, laud, and honor
Unto Christ the King,
This through countless ages
Men and angels sing.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 14: Ringkapha Tui Jesu Amai
lyricist: Fanny J. Crosby (Original) / Rev. William Pettigrew (Trans.)
composer: Phoebe P. Knapp (Tune 873 | Doh is G)
notes: Hymn No. 14 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 3 stanzas with chorus translated by Rev. William Pettigrew.

lines_tangkhul: Chan hi iwaina, la hi phamei,
lines_translation: Blessed assurance, Jesus is mine!
Oh, what a foretaste of glory divine!
Heir of salvation, purchase of God,
Born of His Spirit, washed in His blood.
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior all the day long.
Perfect submission, perfect delight,
Visions of rapture now burst on my sight;
Angels, descending, bring from above
Echoes of mercy, whispers of love.
Perfect submission, all is at rest,
I in my Savior am happy and blest,
Watching and waiting, looking above,
Filled with His goodness, lost in His love.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 17: Arui Ngayali Ili Ngachonlu
title_translation: Abide with Me in Tangkhul Naga
lyricist: Henry F. Lyte (Original) / Rev. William Pettigrew (Trans.)
composer: William H. Monk (Tune 297 | Doh is G)
notes: Hymn No. 17 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 6 complete stanzas translated by Rev. William Pettigrew.

lines_translation: Abide with me, fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens, Lord, with me abide.
When other helpers fail and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, oh, abide with me.
Swift to its close ebbs out life's little day;
Earth's joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.
Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word,
But as Thou dwell'st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free.
Come not to sojourn, but abide with me.
I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter's power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, Lord, abide with me.
I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless;
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death's sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.
Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom and point me to the skies.
Heaven's morning breaks, and earth's vain shadows flee;
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 28: Jesuna Ili Laishi
title_translation: Jesus, Lover of My Soul in Tangkhul Naga
composer: Simeon B. Marsh (Tune 227 | Doh is F)
notes: Hymn No. 28 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 4 complete stanzas translated by Rev. William Pettigrew.

lines_translation: Jesus, Lover of my soul,
Let me to Thy bosom fly,
While the nearer waters roll,
While the tempest still is high.
Hide me, O my Savior, hide,
Till the storm of life is past;
Safe into the haven guide,
Oh, receive my soul at last.
Other refuge have I none,
Hangs my helpless soul on Thee;
Leave, ah! leave me not alone,
Still support and comfort me.
All my trust on Thee is stayed,
All my help from Thee I bring;
Cover my defenseless head
With the shadow of Thy wing.
Thou, O Christ, art all I want;
More than all in Thee I find:
Raise the fallen, cheer the faint,
Heal the sick, and lead the blind.
Just and holy is Thy name,
I am all unrighteousness;
False and full of sin I am;
Thou art full of truth and grace.
Plenteous grace with Thee is found,
Grace to cover all my sin;
Let the healing streams abound,
Make and keep me pure within.
Thou of life the fountain art,
Freely let me take of Thee;
Spring Thou up within my heart,
Rise to all eternity.

title: Jesuwui Laa No. 31: Makashiman Lungkhuri
title_translation: Rock of Ages in Tangkhul Naga
lyricist: Augustus M. Toplady (Original) / Rev. William Pettigrew (Trans.)
notes: Hymn No. 31 from Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga (1907). 4 stanzas translated by Rev. William Pettigrew.

lines_translation: Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee;
Let the water and the blood,
From Thy riven side which flowed,
Be of sin the double cure,
Cleanse me from its guilt and power.
Not the labors of my hands
Can fulfill Thy law's demands;
Could my zeal no respite know,
Could my tears forever flow,
All for sin could not atone;
Thou must save, and Thou alone.
Nothing in my hand I bring,
Simply to Thy cross I cling;
Naked, come to Thee for dress;
Helpless, look to Thee for grace;
Foul, I to the fountain fly;
Wash me, Savior, or I die.
While I draw this fleeting breath,
When mine eyes shall close in death,
When I soar to worlds unknown,
See Thee on Thy judgment throne,
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee.
